verses.text: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle and set apart for God's Good News,
which God had promised long ago through his prophets in the holy Scriptures.
This Good News is about his Son, who in his human life was descended from David,
and who was shown with power to be God's Son by the Spirit of holiness through his resurrection from the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord.
Through him we received grace and the calling to be apostles, so that people among all nations would come to the obedience that faith brings, for the sake of his name.
And you are among them too, called to belong to Jesus Christ.
To everyone in Rome whom God loves and has called to be his holy people: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because people everywhere are talking about your faith.
God, whom I serve with my whole spirit in sharing the Good News about his Son, is my witness that I keep mentioning you in my prayers.
I ask that, if God wills, I may finally be able to visit you.
I really want to see you so I can share some spiritual gift that will help strengthen you,
or, more accurately, so that we can encourage one another through each other's faith, yours and mine.
Brothers and sisters, I don't want you to miss this: I've often planned to visit you, but have been held back until now. I want to see some fruit among you too, just as among the other Gentiles.
I owe this message to Greeks and to people from other cultures, to the educated and the uneducated alike.
So I'm eager to share the Good News with you in Rome too, as far as it depends on me.
I'm not ashamed of the Good News about Christ. It's God's power to save everyone who believes, first the Jew and also the Greek.
In it, God's righteousness is revealed through faith and leads to faith. As Scripture says, ‘The righteous will live by faith.’
God's anger is revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wrongdoing of people who use their wrongdoing to bury the truth.
What can be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them.
Ever since the world was created, God's invisible qualities—his eternal power and divine nature—have been clearly seen in what he made. So people have no excuse.
They knew God, but they didn't honor him as God or thank him. Instead, their thinking became empty, and their foolish hearts went dark.
They claimed to be wise, but became fools,
and traded the glory of the immortal God for images shaped like mortal humans, birds, animals, and reptiles.
So God let them follow the desires of their hearts into impurity, and they dishonored their own bodies among themselves.
They traded God's truth for a lie, and worshiped and served what was created instead of the Creator, who is praised forever. Amen.
Because of this, God let them follow degrading passions. Their women exchanged natural relations for those that go against nature.

In the same way, the men also left natural relations with women and burned with desire for one another. Men did shameful things with men and received in themselves the fitting consequence of their error.
Since they refused to keep God in their knowledge, God let them follow a corrupt way of thinking and do what should not be done.
They became full of every kind of wrongdoing: sexual sin, evil, greed, and malice. They were full of envy, murder, fighting, deceit, and spite; they gossiped,
slandered, hated God, acted arrogantly and abusively, bragged, dreamed up new ways to do evil, and disobeyed their parents.
They were foolish, unfaithful, heartless, and merciless.
They know God's ruling: people who practice these things deserve death. Yet they do them anyway—and even cheer on others who do the same.
